title: Day 8 Knowledge Check: Agentic Workflows, MCP, A2A & RLM

questions.question: How does the Recursive Language Model (RLM) paradigm prevent 'Context Rot' on massive log dumps?

options.A: It stores the long context as an external Python variable, slices it programmatically, and runs sub-SLM calls only on relevant chunks.
options.B: It truncates and discards 95% of the log file randomly.

questions.explanation: RLM treats long context as a programmatic environment rather than stuffing everything into one attention window.
questions.implication: Enables small 1.5B–7B models to inspect multi-megabyte stack traces accurately without needle-in-a-haystack degradation.

questions.question: What is the architectural difference between MCP and the A2A v1.0 protocol?

options.A: MCP connects an agent vertically to tools/APIs; A2A v1.0 connects independent agents horizontally via Agent Cards without sharing internal memory.
options.B: MCP is only for Java; A2A is only for CSS.
options.C: They are identical names for SQLite.

questions.explanation: MCP standardizes tool/data access, while A2A v1.0 standardizes cross-agent discovery and task delegation.
questions.implication: Using both protocols lets your SRE agent query internal MCP tools while collaborating safely with external FinOps or Security agents.

questions.question: Why enforce deterministic bounds (like max_steps) on autonomous ReAct agents?

options.A: To prevent infinite tool-calling loops, runaway latency, and unexpected cloud API spend.
options.B: Because Python loops cannot run more than twice.

questions.explanation: Deterministic step budgets guarantee predictable worst-case latency and cost.
questions.implication: Unbounded while-True agent loops are a top cause of production outages and surprise token bills.
